name: D₄
notes: The eight symmetries of a square: four rotations (e, r, r², r³) and four reflections (f, rf, r²f, r³f). Extraction is cheap here — you can do it with a piece of paper, which is exactly what makes it a better first non-abelian group than Q₈. Presentation: ⟨r, f | r⁴ = f² = e, frf = r⁻¹⟩. That last relation is the one that makes it non-abelian: pushing a rotation through a flip reverses it. Note the naming hazard — some authors write D₄ (indexing by the polygon's sides), others D₈ (by the number of elements). Same group either way.
